answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each identity holds a trust score that decays without fresh verified interactions, and new identities start at the curve's floor, so spawning many yields near-zero influence. Attacker cost is the sustained work of maintaining each sparrow identity above threshold. Cross-agent endorsements form a grove of linked records that raises the marginal cost of the next fake identity. A cipher ties each endorsement to prior interaction history, so buying support requires real activity, paid per identity.
